CITY OF BEVERLY HILLS
  455 N. Rexford Drive
  Beverly Hills, CA 90210
  Room 280A
  Beverly Hills City Council Liaison / Public Works Commission Meeting

  SPECIAL MEETING HIGHLIGHTS

  Wednesday, May 31, 2023
  11:30 AM

MEETING CALLED TO ORDER
Date / Time:  May 31, 2023 / 11:35 AM

IN ATTENDANCE:  Mayor Julian Gold MD, Councilmember Sharona Nazarian PYSD, Public
  Works Commissioner John Millan, Public Works Director Shana Epstein,
  Assistant City Manager Ryan Gohlich, Assistant Finance Director Tatiana
  Szerwinski, Senior Management Analyst Melissa Gomez, Executive
  Assistant Ilene Knebel, Rick Simonson (HF&H Consultants LLC)

1. PUBLIC COMMENT

  Members of the public will be given the opportunity to directly address the Committee on any
  item listed on the agenda.

  Speakers:  David Gingold

2. STATUS UPDATE FOR THE WATER AND WASTEWATER COST OF SERVICE STUDY
  Public Works Director Shana Epstein gave a presentation on the proposed water and
  wastewater rates, including for water, fund balance projections, water tier adjustments,
  proposed water quantity rates and service charges, and comparisons with other agencies. For
  wastewater, the presentation covered the fund balance, return to sewer factors, single-family
  irrigation customer analysis, proposed wastewater rates, various customer bills with phase in,
  wastewater rates phased-in, and comparisons with other agencies. Combined bill impacts for
  all customer classes were also presented. Staff is not asking for a revenue increase in
  wastewater. The proposed wastewater cost of service rates would see single and multi-family
  bi-monthly fixed service charges decrease with the introduction of a flow-based quantity
  charge. Staff recommended that the Liaison review and provide direction on the proposed
  rate changes and policy recommendations.

  The liaison asked about fluctuations in water bills, the effect of federal grants on the water
  fund balance, and the accounting behind the proposals. After discussion, the liaison approved
  moving forward the proposed water and wastewater rates to the full City Council for approval
  to notify the community following Proposition 218 guidelines. The plan is to present to the
  City Council at a study session in the summer, with a public hearing in October. Community
  outreach will be conducted in August and September. The schedule will be shared once
  finalized. If approved by the City Council, adjusted wastewater rates and the adjusted water
  reliability charge would become effective January 1, 2024, and adjusted water rates would
  become effective January 1, 2025.

ADJOURNMENT
Date / Time:  May 31, 2023 / 12:23 PM
